summary: Fresh packet-bound Q4 review completed from scratch at task commit 3a463000607f2dcdf88785a77d2dc5767f473e05. The instruction and delegated runtime contract cover a coherent engineering objective and the verifier has substantial independent coverage, but bidirectional alignment is not complete. Eleven material blocking findings remain: solver-visible implementation-diagnosis leakage; material movement/catalog policy gaps; transfer valuation/availability gaps; incomplete cross-generation replay verification; incomplete detailed-settlement safety verification; archive verification that lacks an adversarial independent negative case; incomplete preflight/audit operational-domain verification; non-public internal Python API coupling; an overbroad no-generation-id-in-any-JSONL assertion; grading-relevant ambiguity in item-policy semantics; and incomplete successful rejected-movement durability verification. One LOW advisory notes evaluation-framed wording. All 40 verifier tests and all material instruction/runtime-contract requirement families were inventoried in both directions, and the second adversarial omission sweep completed.

findings.criterion: No unnecessary solver-visible implementation diagnosis or repair map
findings.why_it_matters: Multiple solver-visible comments name the exact defective condition and the intended correction: zero quantity, MOVE transfer-loop exception, inactive-item/destination status omissions, layout omission from generation identity, the compound resume predicate, the resume off-by-one, the replay-boundary predicate, the wrong transfer effect-kind selector, the plural effect-count key, the permissive publication gate, idempotency collision handling, and copytree promotion. These are not architecture/API/runbook documentation; they collapse diagnosis work and expose the repair topology.
findings.minimal_remediation: Remove or rewrite defect-specific comments so they document intended invariant/domain semantics without identifying the current faulty branch, predicate, key, or replacement mechanism. Preserve ordinary code readability and the solver-visible functional contracts.
findings.regression_risk: Low if only diagnosis comments are neutralized; do not remove legitimate contract documentation or change runtime behavior in this remediation.

findings.criterion: Every material movement-shape, item-policy and warehouse-policy requirement is semantically verified
findings.why_it_matters: The instruction requires exact source/destination shape by movement type, item existence, item active status, item max_unit_cost and quantity_precision policy, and existence/active status for every referenced warehouse. Current tests cover valid reason/type combinations, several invalid reason/type combinations, zero quantity, same-warehouse transfer, inactive item and inactive receipt destination, but do not exercise the prohibited/missing source/destination shapes, unknown item, unknown warehouse, max_unit_cost or quantity_precision behavior. A solver can omit those material acceptance/rejection rules and still pass.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add independent behavioral cases for each unverified material policy boundary, using CLI/pipeline behavior where possible rather than only internal helper calls.
findings.regression_risk: Policy tests must preserve the documented valid cases and avoid inventing new reject-code contracts for item/warehouse unknown cases unless those codes are made solver-visible.

findings.criterion: Weighted valuation and available-quantity requirements are tested for each materially distinct movement boundary
findings.why_it_matters: Issue valuation is independently pinned to source weighted cost, but transfer valuation is checked only by asserting that the two transfer values net to zero. An implementation that prices both transfer legs from the movement-supplied unit cost can satisfy that assertion while violating source-weighted valuation. Available-quantity coverage is also issue-centric; transfer overdraw is not independently exercised. These are observable inventory-value/safety requirements.
findings.minimal_remediation: For transfer, assert the absolute source-weighted value carried by both legs as well as zero net value, and exercise a transfer whose requested quantity exceeds available source quantity. Add any other distinct valuation boundary that the instruction intends to grade.
findings.regression_risk: Keep receipt/issue/adjustment semantics separate; do not accidentally force movement unit cost to be ignored where the documented contract intends it to be used.

findings.criterion: Current-generation replay suppression and cross-generation non-duplication are behaviorally verified
findings.why_it_matters: The pipeline rerun test covers same-generation replay suppression, and the database test proves the schema permits the same movement_id in another generation. It does not exercise the processing/replay guard across two generations. A globally keyed replay guard can therefore reject a legitimate movement in a new source/layout/date generation while all current tests still pass.
findings.minimal_remediation: Process the same movement identity in two distinct generation identities and verify the second generation is accepted/applied independently while same-generation replay remains suppressed.
findings.regression_risk: Ensure the added test changes a documented generation component and does not merely insert rows directly into the database.

findings.criterion: Every detailed-settlement publication blocker is independently tested
findings.why_it_matters: The verifier exercises missing accepted effects, unbalanced transfers, duplicate movement identities/orphan effects, and negative quantity. It does not independently create duplicate effect_kind rows for one movement or a position whose quantity is non-negative while value is below -0.01. A solver can omit either documented settlement invariant and still pass, allowing unsafe publication/audit behavior.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add independent negative cases for duplicate effect kinds and negative inventory value below the documented threshold, and verify both reconciliation/audit detection and publication blocking where the contract makes them gates.
findings.regression_risk: Isolate quantity and value failures so one invariant cannot mask the other.

findings.criterion: Archive verification is independently verified rather than accepted from a healthy/self-reported path
findings.why_it_matters: Archive is required to verify report/publication contracts and create a verified archive. The archive workflow is only invoked on healthy inputs. The verifier checks returned passed=true plus the presence of controls/delta/lineage strings and later registry/audit evidence, but it never corrupts a report/publication input before archive and requires archive to fail, nor independently validates the generated archive's integrity structure. A solver can substantially weaken the archive verification gate and still satisfy the happy-path evidence.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add at least one independently corrupted report/publication negative case that archive must reject without a visible successful archive/registry event, and independently validate the generated archive integrity/lineage evidence rather than relying only on archive's own passed flag and embedded strings.
findings.regression_risk: Do not conflate audit's publication corruption check with archive verification; archive needs its own negative boundary.

findings.criterion: Delegated preflight and audit operational domains are meaningfully exercised and stable health output is verified
findings.why_it_matters: Preflight's schema, framing, catalog, historical baseline and recovery domains are substantively tested, but the batch-window probe only requires a payload difference for another business date; generation identity alone makes that payload differ without proving batch-window evaluation. Authorization/safety state is not independently varied. Audit corruption cases cover many domains, but the contract says audit exposes accounting and other named health domains while tests mostly assert passed/failed and payload inequality, not the presence/meaning of the stable health surface. These operational requirements can change observable correctness and operator interface behavior.
findings.minimal_remediation: Use independent state/input mutations whose only relevant effect is the delegated batch-window/authorization/safety domain, and assert semantically meaningful audit health fields for each documented operator domain, especially accounting, without over-specifying incidental formatting.
findings.regression_risk: Avoid asserting volatile timestamps or implementation-only field ordering; grade stable semantic health signals.

findings.criterion: Verifier must not require undocumented/non-public implementation API topology when public behavior is the contract
findings.why_it_matters: The solver-visible request explicitly preserves the public executable and CLI/state contracts, while src.__all__ exposes only PipelineConfig, process and main. The verifier nevertheless imports numerous non-exported module-local types/functions directly from accounting, checkpoint, comp3, database, framing, generation, layout, models, policy, publication, reconciliation and reconciliation_detail. A behaviorally conforming repair that legitimately refactors those internal modules/signatures can fail before public behavior is evaluated.
findings.minimal_remediation: Move material grading toward the public CLI/durable-state interfaces, or explicitly designate any Python APIs that truly must remain stable as solver-visible inherited interfaces. Retain direct unit tests only where the API itself is part of the contract.
findings.regression_risk: Do not weaken semantic precision: public-path tests may still create controlled DB/state fixtures and independently inspect durable outputs.

findings.criterion: Negative verifier assertions must match the documented publication boundary and not forbid legitimate diagnostics
findings.why_it_matters: On failed reconciliation the test correctly requires no visible publication directory, but additionally asserts that the generation id appears in no *.jsonl anywhere under the temporary work root. The contract forbids publication, not diagnostic/audit/quarantine JSONL evidence that records a failed generation. A conforming implementation can therefore fail for emitting legitimate failure evidence unrelated to publication.
findings.minimal_remediation: Scope the assertion to publication-registry/publication-success evidence, or otherwise identify the specific JSONL artifact whose absence constitutes non-publication. Permit legitimate failure/audit/quarantine records.
findings.regression_risk: Keep the strong no-visible-publication assertion and ensure failed generations are never registered as successfully published.

findings.criterion: Grading-relevant item-policy semantics must have a single solver-visible authority
findings.why_it_matters: The instruction says item-policy decisions use items.active, items.max_unit_cost and items.quantity_precision, but it does not state the acceptance rule for max_unit_cost or whether quantity_precision means reject excess scale, round/quantize, or another policy. The delegated runtime contract does not resolve these two fields. Because these are material acceptance rules, different reasonable implementations can disagree on observable correctness.
findings.minimal_remediation: State the functional acceptance semantics for max_unit_cost and quantity_precision in the solver-visible work request or a legitimate referenced policy contract, without naming the module/function to change.
findings.regression_risk: Specify behavior, not implementation mechanics or hidden test examples.

findings.criterion: Successful rejected-movement durability must verify all documented durable components, not rollback alone
findings.why_it_matters: The rejection rollback test proves reject/processed/checkpoint/event state rolls back when the REJECT journal insertion aborts, and other cases prove a reject row/code can persist. No successful rejected-movement case independently verifies that the checkpoint advances and the journal event is durable (and that processed status is durable where applicable). An implementation can omit successful checkpoint advancement while still pass the current rejection tests, breaking restart safety.
findings.minimal_remediation: After a successful policy/accounting rejection and after a framing/transform rejection as applicable, inspect durable checkpoint and journal state and verify the documented sequence/fingerprint advancement together with the reject/processed rows.
findings.regression_risk: Respect the contract's 'processed-row status when applicable' distinction for decode/transform failures.

findings.criterion: Solver-facing prose should describe engineering authority rather than benchmark evaluation framing
findings.why_it_matters: The phrase 'movement-shape authority for grading is functional' is evaluation-framed language in an otherwise production-style handoff. It does not expose a hidden test, but it is unnecessary benchmark framing.
findings.minimal_remediation: Rephrase as an engineering authority statement, for example that the listed functional movement rules are authoritative, without mentioning grading.
findings.regression_risk: None if only wording changes and the same functional rules remain.
